steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Selection criteria: function, aesthetics, cost (material + processing + assembly), availability, sustainability (recyclability, material miles), manufacturability. | Key Fact: Decision matrix: weighted scoring system - list criteria, assign weights, score each option, multiply weight x score, total reveals best choice. Removes bias. | Key Fact: Working properties must match function: frying pan handle needs thermal insulation (thermoset/silicone), not conductivity (metal). Bicycle frame needs strength-to-weight (aluminium/CFRP). | Key Fact: Batch vs mass production affects material choice: mass production justifies injection moulding tooling; batch uses CNC or hand-laid composites.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Create a simple decision matrix to compare acrylic, polycarbonate and glass for a display cabinet door. | A designer must choose between aluminium and polypropylene for a kitchen utensil handle. Justify using at least four criteria. | Explain how production volume (batch vs mass) influences material selection for a plastic product.
